input.quote: 13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer.
input.rationale: The grant clause meets the preferred position, not merely the fallback: § 13.1 extends the subscription grant to Customer's Affiliates and to contractors acting on their behalf (no written-notice precondition needed); § 13.2 gives Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, fully paid licence to delivered software and Vendor Technology, including Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable, with contractor support rights; and § 13.3 permits transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor under the Section 24 assignment rights and bars revocation or suspension except for a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity. The § 13.4 use restrictions are ordinary and carved back for lawful testing and Customer Data. Noted but not flagged here: § 14.2 gives only a "revocable, non-transferable" term-limited licence to Deliverables themselves; that outlier is constrained by § 13.3's no-revocation and transfer provisions and by § 14.3's cross-reference to the § 13.2 perpetual licence, and the Deliverable ownership/scope point is addressed under the IP rule rather than double-flagged here.
